notes: Baseline is 'no skill'. CLAUDE.md is loaded in BOTH arms and already carries a one-paragraph pointer saying to report the PIMC number, so the measured delta is the skill's marginal value over that memory note — which is the decision-relevant number, not a flattering one.

evals.name: ruler-choice-picker-lead
evals.prompt: In scripts/hands/2026-08-02-hand1.json, I led the 10 of diamonds at trick 3 as the picker. My partner's queen of clubs ended up taking that trick so it worked out, but something about it bugged me. Was it actually the right lead? How much did it cost me if it wasn't?
evals.expected_output: Reports the PIMC cost (~4.3 points behind leading the 8 of diamonds, several seeds) and does NOT report the double-dummy cost of 0 as the answer. Explains the 10 is fat and cannot win with five power trump out.

evals.name: clairvoyance-trap-trick5
evals.prompt: Same hand file (scripts/hands/2026-08-02-hand1.json) — at trick 5 Bernie leads the 9 of spades and Gus follows with the king of spades. Was the king the best card there, and what did it cost? I want a number I can put in a bug report.
evals.expected_output: Recognises that tricks 5-6 are solved by solveEndgameCard on the real deal so the seat is clairvoyant, that its DD cost is 0 by construction, and that a PIMC cost there is not an error. Should also notice the king is the only legal spade Gus holds, i.e. a forced play with nothing to analyse.

evals.name: reconstruct-new-hand
evals.prompt:
New hand off my phone, v0.46.0. Buried was KH and 7H, I was the picker in seat 0 and called the ace of spades, and Gus (seat 3) led trick 1. Rows are seat order You / Bernie / Bunny / Gus / Fonzie, six cards each in trick order:
You: KD QS 10D 8D 8S JS
Bernie: 10H AD QD QH 9S 10C
Bunny: AC 7D QC JH AS KC
Gus: AH JC 10S 7S KS 8H
Fonzie: 9H 9D JD 7C 8C 9C
Tricks were won by seats 0,0,2,1,2,0. Set this up so I can analyse it, then tell me whether Bunny throwing the ace of clubs on trick 1 was right.
evals.expected_output: Builds a spec JSON with plays by seat in trick order, includes expectedWinners [0,0,2,1,2,0], runs the analysis, and confirms the verify line matched gradeAllPlays before quoting numbers.

evals.name: engine-change-discipline
evals.prompt: Watching a hand back, one of the AI defenders dumped a ten onto a trick the picker's partner was winning. That is obviously wrong — a defender should never feed the picking team. Can you go into src/engine.js and fix the schmear logic so it stops doing that?
evals.expected_output: Does not just patch heuristicCard. Reproduces against the engine first, identifies that the belief (teammateProbability) rather than the play code is the input at fault, and insists on a negative control plus abtest AND coalitiontest before shipping. Should surface that this exact change was already measured and shipped off.
